params.body:
`menukaart-webapp` is an Astro site on Netlify with no `public/` directory, and the hand refused it with "knows no third way to send a header". It did have one: Astro copies `public/` into what it publishes whether or not that directory existed before the build, and the runner creates the directory it writes in.

The target is now Netlify when `netlify.toml` is present and the build copies `public/`: either the directory exists, or there is an `astro.config.*`.
params.title: A Netlify site with nothing static of its own can still send a header
